thread:
Elaine: quick PR check  Security > Audit Logs section. Legal flagged the phrase 'Redwood is SOC2 certified' as risky. Proposed replacement: 'Redwood's controls are designed to align with SOC 2 trust service criteria and undergo regular independent assessment.' I also added a short, ops-friendly export example and a tiny SDK call. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/1555

Patrick: that wording works for me. can we add a one-line note about where to request the attestation (support@redwood.com) and call out default retention values? engineers want concrete defaults.

Elaine: added: 'Default hosted-audit retention: 90 days. Dedicated/Private: tenant-configurable and may be subject to contract terms.' Also pasted the examples below. please scan for tone and linter cleanliness.

Juan: examples look good overall. two nits: 1) avoid inline comments inside code blocks. 2) use boolean for flags in JSON. otherwise +1.

Elaine: updated. BEFORE event (raw ingest):
```json
{
  "id": "evt_2027_0007",
  "user": { "id": "user_99", "email": "sam@org.com" },
  "action": "session.create",
  "ts": "2027-03-02T11:00:00Z"
}
```
AFTER event (export with pseudonymization):
```json
{
  "id": "evt_2027_0007",
  "user": { "id": "anon_abc123", "email": "REDACTED" },
  "action": "session.create",
  "ts": "2027-03-02T11:00:00Z",
  "pseudonymized": true
}
```
CLI export example (request anonymized JSONL):
```bash
redwood-cli audit export --from 2027-01-01 --to 2027-02-28 --anonymize --format jsonl --out /tmp/audit-jan-feb.jsonl
```
Python SDK sample (pseudo):
```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_KEY}")
client.log_event({"event_type": "session.create"}, retention_ttl="90d", pseudonymize_fields=["user.email"]) 
```
Elaine: added one-line note for customers: 'For attestation copies or customized export procedures, contact support@redwood.com.'

Sara: Legal ACK for the phrasing and contact line. small edit: prefer 'SOC 2' (with a space) in the final doc. also ok with the defaults.

Patrick: CI note  docs linter sometimes rejects unlabeled code fences. make sure each fence uses json, bash or python. docs-ci-bot will catch it.

docs-ci-bot: PR check queued. lint error (example): code-block language tag missing on one fence. See CI: https://ci.redwood.example/1555/logs

Elaine: thanks bot, fixed all fences and removed comments. will merge after CI passes and final legal confirmation. Thanks everyone :tada:
